7.1.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "what causes aseptic loosening of a THA?"
- "**Wear → particulate debris → osteolysis → loosening**: a late, cumulative failure of a well-fixed implant."
- "Causes → **mechanical**, **biological**, **technical** · exclude **infection** first (→ 6 Periprosthetic Infection)."
- "Cemented stems fail in **Gruen's 4 modes** → pistoning, medial midstem pivot, calcar pivot, bending cantilever."

### Definition & significance
- Loosening definition, septic vs aseptic split → 6 Periprosthetic Infection
- Aseptic form is **cumulative** → the long-term fate of a well-fixed implant

CLINICAL PEARL — the cup loosens silently
- **Acetabular** loosening is often **asymptomatic** → only serial X-rays find it
- Follow-up → **yearly**, then every **3 years**, then every **3–5 years** (Prof Sherif Khaled)

[[FIG: Fig 7.1 · 7.1

### Aetiology — three layers
| Cause | Examples |
|---|---|
| **Mechanical** | acute or repeated trauma · extreme ROM (range of motion) · prior dislocation · old fracture |
| **Biological** | unhealthy bed: irradiated, diseased, brittle · wear-induced **osteolysis** |
| **Technical** | thin **cement mantle** (→ 2 Fixation) · **varus** stem, lateralised tip · instability · poor fracture fixation |

- Chain → varus stem → bending stress → micromotion + debris → osteolysis
- Early **subsidence** of a cementless stem → technical: undersizing, no initial press-fit
- **Young, heavy, active** patients → higher long-term loosening
- Case → **composite-beam** cemented stem at 16 years: cement gone, zone 1 only → subsidence
[[FIG: Fig 7.2 · 7.1

### Wear-debris osteolysis
- **Wear** definition and modes → 1 Implants
- **Osteolysis** = host bone response to debris → silent, extensive on film before pain
- Time-dependent, mainly **cell-mediated** inflammation driven by debris
[[FIG: Fig 7.3 · 7.1
- Sources → **polyethylene** commonest · cobalt, titanium, **cement** · wear and corrosion particles

#### Cells & mediators
- **Submicron** particles (<1 µm) → phagocytosed by **macrophages** → most active (Miller)
- Mediators → interleukins incl. **IL-6**, prostaglandin → bone-resorbing cytokines
- **RANKL** → osteoclast activation → resorption → micromotion → more wear: vicious cycle
- Drugs → bisphosphonates, denosumab hit the osteoclast · established lysis → remove the debris source

### Effective joint space
- Debris → raised **hydrostatic pressure** → fluid creeps into every interface = **effective joint space**
- Hence lysis far from the bearing → stem tip, behind the cup, screw holes
[[FIG: Fig 7.4 · 7.1
- Tracks along **bone–cement** or **bone–prosthesis** · **circumferential** proximal coating seals it
- On film → **linear** lucency = loosening · **expansile, scalloped** = particle osteolysis

### Gruen's modes of stem failure
| Mode (cemented stem) | Where fixation is lost | Picture |
|---|---|---|
| **1A Pistoning** | stem sinks inside the cement | mantle stable |
| **1B Pistoning** | stem + cement sink in bone | commonest cemented |
| **2 Medial midstem pivot** | fixed mid-stem, loose above and below | lucency superomedial + inferolateral |
| **3 Calcar pivot** | fixed proximally, loose distally | **windshield wiper** → distal ballooning |
| **4 Bending cantilever** | fixed distally, loose proximally | **stem fracture** |

- **Stem fracture** = sure sign of a loose cemented stem → cantilever mechanism (Prof Sherif Khaled)
[[FIG: Fig 7.5 · 7.1
- Definite signs → broken stem, cement fracture, stem–cement lucency, change in position
[[FIG: Fig 7.6 · 7.1
- Drawings → where lucency and cement fracture appear in each pattern
[[FIG: Fig 7.7–7.8 · 7.1

#### Measured & visible signs
- **Subsidence** → 1–2 mm in year 1 normal · **2–5 mm** concern (Prof Sherif Khaled)
[[FIG: Fig 7.9 · 7.1
- Measure → greater-trochanter tip or head–neck junction to stem tip, identical serial films
- Pivot → swings and erodes one side · **wiper** → fixed proximally, distal toggle
[[FIG: Fig 7.10 · 7.1
- Case → construct subsided, stem pistoned, **cement fractured** · distal opacity = cement plug · pedestal → cementless only
[[FIG: Fig 7.11 · 7.1

- **Wear → debris → macrophage → RANKL → lysis · pressure spreads it · 4 Gruen modes, cantilever breaks the stem**

7.2.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "how do you diagnose aseptic loosening?"
- "**Start-up** and weight-bearing pain = aseptic · **night** pain = septic · groin = cup, thigh = stem."
- "Bloods (ESR, CRP) ± aspirate to **exclude infection**; then serial films for **lucency** and **migration**."
- "Cemented stem → **Harris** grades · cementless → **Engh** · cup → lucency **>2 mm in 3 zones**."

### Clinical picture
- Primary goal → **exclude septic loosening** · **groin** pain → cup · **thigh** pain → stem
- **Aseptic** → activity pain, **start-up pain**, worse on weight bearing → loose implant settles
- **Septic** → constant pain, **worse at night**, most afebrile (Prof Sherif Khaled)
- Examine → gait, ROM, **LLD** (leg-length discrepancy), neurology, prior dislocation, obesity

PITFALL — thigh pain is not always a loose stem
- Well-fixed cementless stem → **modulus mismatch**: stiff tip in a flexible femur · spine and knee mimic hip pain
- Say → "**examine the spine and knee, and check fixation, before blaming the stem**"

### Laboratory work-up
- Bloods, aspiration and their traps → 6 Periprosthetic Infection

#### At revision
- **Antibiotics withheld** until cultures return · except one dose pre-op + one post-op (Prof Sherif Khaled)
[[FIG: Fig 7.12 · 7.2
- Tissue → Gram stain, aerobic, anaerobic · **TB** in chronic referred cases · serial ESR/CRP
[[FIG: Fig 7.13 · 7.2

### Radiographic signs
- **AP + lateral** to the stem tip · accuracy femoral **90%**, acetabular **65%** (Prof Sherif Khaled)
- Signs → **lucency** (most important), **migration** (most reliable), implant or cement fracture
- **Thin sclerotic line** beside a stable lucency = fibrous border · **periosteal reaction** → think infection
- **Arthrography** or **CT** → lucencies hidden behind metal

#### Cemented stem — Harris grades
| Grade | Sign (Campbell) |
|---|---|
| **Possible** | incomplete lucency, **>50%** of the cement interface |
| **Probable** | **complete** lucency around the cement |
| **Definite** | stem or cement fracture · stem–cement lucency · change in stem position |

- Lucent lines → incomplete · complete around the stem
[[FIG: Fig 7.14–7.15 · 7.2
- Case → **lateral mantle fracture** + lines almost all round → definitely loose, asymptomatic → followed
[[FIG: Fig 7.16 · 7.2

#### Cup loosening
- **Cementless** → migration >2–5 mm · lines in **3 zones**, >2 mm, progressive over 2 years (Prof Sherif Khaled)
- Also → **inclination change** alone · screw breakage · medialisation · protrusio
- **Cemented** → lucency all round, >2 mm, progressive, 3 zones · superior or medial migration · wear
[[FIG: Fig 7.17 · 7.2
- Loose cementless cup + **cavitary defect** → **CT** for the medial wall
[[FIG: Fig 7.18–7.19 · 7.2

### Interpreting radiolucency
- **Cement–metal** lucency → always loosening: nothing debonds normally
- **Cement–bone** or cementless → counts only if **>2 mm** and **progressive** · stable = benign or design
- Case → lines in 50–100% of interface, unchanged at 5 years → **poor cementing**
- Polished taper-slip (**Exeter**) → small early shoulder gap expected, not loosening

#### Zones
- Gruen and DeLee–Charnley zones → 3 Planning

#### Engh grades — cementless stem
| Grade | Signs (Prof Sherif Khaled) |
|---|---|
| **Stable bony ingrowth** → fixed | **spot welds**, reactive bone lines · calcar atrophy (stress shielding), no pedestal |
| **Stable fibrous** → stable | no spot welds, no migration · **parallel sclerotic lines** |
| **Unstable fibrous** → loose | **progressive** lines · subsidence, varus drift · **pedestal** at the tip |

- Bony ingrowth → **spot welds**: endosteal bone bridging to the coating, near an extensive coating's end
[[FIG: Fig 7.20 · 7.2
- Unstable → progressive lines, subsidence · **pedestal** = bone stopping the tip
[[FIG: Fig 7.21–7.22 · 7.2
- Thin proximal bone + distal spot welds = **load bypass**, not loosening → well fixed
[[FIG: Fig 7.51 · 7.2

### Nuclear scans
- Technetium vs indium scans → 6 Periprosthetic Infection

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "how do you classify bone loss at revision?"
- "**Paprosky** → what host bone is left to hold the implant · drives the treatment."
- "**D'Antonio (AAOS)** → **segmental** (uncontained) vs **cavitary** (contained), combined, discontinuity, arthrodesis."
- "Contained → morselised graft · uncontained → structural support · plan with **CT**."

### Two systems
- **Paprosky** → anatomical, most used for surgical decisions
- **AAOS** (American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons) → by location, descriptive
- **Contained** (cavitary) → morselised graft · **uncontained** (segmental) → structural support

#### Imaging before reconstruction
- **AP + lateral + Judet** views · **CT** axial + coronal in every complex case (Prof Hazem)
[[FIG: Fig 7.23 · 7.3
- **Axial** → walls, columns, floor thickness → how far to ream
[[FIG: Fig 7.24 · 7.3
- **Coronal** → superior cover · cup **>50% uncovered** → reconstruct (Prof Hazem)
- **3D CT** → best picture of the defect
[[FIG: Fig 7.25 · 7.3

### Paprosky — acetabulum
| Type | Findings (Campbell) |
|---|---|
| **1** | supportive rim, no lysis, no migration |
| **2** | distorted hemisphere, columns intact, migration **<2 cm** → **2A** superomedial · **2B** superolateral, no dome · **2C** medial only |
| **3A** | migration **>2 cm** "up and out" · **Köhler intact** · 30–60% of cup on graft · loss 10 to 2 o'clock |
| **3B** | migration >2 cm "up and in" · **Köhler broken** · >60% on graft · loss 9 to 5 o'clock · discontinuity |

- Course version → type 1 rim intact · 2 superior involvement · 3 migrated
- Four signs → superior migration · **ischial** lysis (posterior column) · **teardrop** lysis (medial wall) · **Köhler** breach
[[FIG: Fig 7.26 · 7.3

### Paprosky — femur
| Type | Bone left (Campbell) |
|---|---|
| **1** | minimal metaphyseal loss, diaphysis intact |
| **2** | extensive metaphyseal loss, diaphysis intact |
| **3A** | metaphysis unsupportive · **>4 cm** intact diaphysis |
| **3B** | metaphysis unsupportive · **<4 cm** intact diaphysis |
| **4** | metaphysis + diaphysis lost, wide canal, isthmus unsupportive |

- Key variable → length of intact **isthmus** for distal fixation
[[FIG: Fig 7.27 · 7.3
- **Modular tapered fluted titanium** stems → 3A and 3B · grip a short diaphysis

### AAOS (D'Antonio) — acetabulum
| Type | Defect |
|---|---|
| **I Segmental** | rim lost → **uncontained** |
| **II Cavitary** | volume lost, rim kept → **contained** |
| **III Combined** | segmental + cavitary |
| **IV Pelvic discontinuity** | superior and inferior halves separated |
| **V Arthrodesis** | fused hip → excess bone, not deficiency |

- I and II → **peripheral** (anterior, superior, posterior) or **central** (floor) (Prof Hazem)
[[FIG: Fig 7.28–7.29 · 7.3
- Type V → find the **true acetabulum**: teardrop, obturator foramen · assess abductors first

- **Extended trochanteric osteotomy** → access + corrects proximal deformity

7.4.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "how do you reconstruct a deficient acetabulum and femur?"
- "Cup needs **≥50% living host bone** → contained: ream, bigger cup ± graft · uncontained: augment, allograft or cage."
- "Discontinuity → **stabilise first** → plate, cup-cage, triflange or distraction."
- "Femur → fix where good bone is: metaphysis → diaphysis → **impaction grafting**, composite or **proximal femoral replacement**."

### Acetabulum — goals
- Restore hip centre → lower joint reaction force · host-bone contact · good cup position (Prof Hazem)
[[FIG: Fig 7.32 · 7.4
- Graft only fills space → cup on graft migrates · contact **posterior column and rim**

### Acetabulum — contained defects
- **Type 1** → ream, larger porous cup (**jumbo**) · graft optional
- **Type 2** (A, B, C) → larger porous cup + **graft mandatory** · 2C: particulate, block, wafered head
- **Small cavitary** → ignore · cup ≈1 mm larger (Prof Hazem)
[[FIG: Fig 7.33 · 7.4
- **Large cavitary**, e.g. protrusio → morselised graft 3–5 mm, **impaction grafting**
[[FIG: Fig 7.34 · 7.4

#### Extensive cavitary & jumbo cup
- **Flanged** cup, more screws, **Müller ring** → protects graft until incorporation
[[FIG: Fig 7.35 · 7.4
- Rule → **≥50%** of the porous surface on host bone (Prof Hazem)
- **Jumbo cup** ≈66–80 mm → more host contact · may raise centre, removes bone (Surgery of the Hip)
[[FIG: Fig 7.36 · 7.4

### Acetabulum — uncontained defects
- **Type 3** → structural allograft (figure-7 distal femur), **augments** or **cage**
- **Anterior or inferior** segment → ignore if bone good · **superior or posterior** → main support → reconstruct
[[FIG: Fig 7.37 · 7.4
- Allograft with screws or augments → **uncontained → contained** (Prof Hazem)
[[FIG: Fig 7.38–7.39 · 7.4
- **Combined** → segmental first (→ contained), then cavitary
[[FIG: Fig 7.40 · 7.4

- Handbook → always cemented · Campbell → porous-metal augment + **cementless** cup, cement only joins them
- Say → "**cementless cup on augments; cemented cup inside a cage or on bulk allograft**"

### Pelvic discontinuity
- No durable cup until both halves unite → **stabilise first**, then cup or ring (Prof Hazem)
[[FIG: Fig 7.41 · 7.4
- Suspect → broken **obturator ring**, hemipelves rotated on Judet views

| Type | Management |
|---|---|
| **1** | ream → larger stem, no graft |
| **2** | larger porous stem → proximal **or** extensive coating |
| **3A** | extensively coated stem **mandatory** → distal fixation |
